issues.detail: The Hebrew 'וַיִּוָּעַץ אֶל עֲבָדָיו לֵאמֹר' means 'he took counsel with his servants, saying' (i.e., he consulted/planned with them), but the Chinese '對他的僕人出謀劃策說' renders it as 'he gave counsel/plans to his servants, saying,' reversing the direction of the counsel (from the king to his servants rather than with them). This changes who is doing the advising.
